assessments.task_description:
Task Description

Effective mental health practice requires clinicians to communicate clinical information clearly in both written and verbal formats. This assessment is designed to support students in developing advanced skills in report writing and case consultation whilst using a CBT framework. For this task, there are two interrelated components:

  1. A written case report, where you will present a detailed account of your clinical work (or a fictionalised equivalent) with a client, family, or group using a cognitive behavioural therapy (CBT) framework.
  2. A brief case conference, where you will discuss your case with peers and the teaching team in a format that mirrors collaborative mental health practice.

The written case report should include:

  • A 1 paragraph overview of the client and presenting issues
  • The assessment process and key findings
  • A CBT-based case formulation
  • A proposed treatment plan linked to the formulation
  • A brief rationale for observed or anticipated outcomes

Brief case conference:

Following submission of the written case report, you will participate in a brief case conference during class time. You will provide a concise overview of the case before discussing a clinical challenge, treatment decision, adaptation, or area of uncertainty relevant to the case.

The purpose of the case conference is to develop professional consultation skills, whilst providing an opportunity to justify the clinical reasoning.

The oral presentation will be recorded for eventual review purposes.

Assessment Criteria

PART 1 and 2: Detailed criteria and a more detailed rubric will be available to students on Blackboard.

You will be assessed on your:

  • Application of CBT assessment, formulation, and treatment planning principles
  • Clarity, consistency and structure of written communication
  • Clinical reasoning and justification of treatment decisions
  • Professional communication and participation in the brief case conference
  • Ability to discuss and respond to questions regarding the case

Academic Integrity Note

This assessment includes both a written and oral component. Students may use resources, including AI, in the preparation of the written case report, provided all use is appropriately acknowledged in accordance with University guidelines.

The brief case conference provides an opportunity for students to demonstrate and discuss their own clinical reasoning in relation to the assessment findings, formulation, and treatment plan presented in their report. Students should therefore ensure they are familiar with and able to justify the content of their submission.

assessments.task_description:
Task Description

Effective CBT practice requires clinicians to move beyond understanding therapeutic concepts and demonstrate the ability to apply interventions in a collaborative, flexible, and responsive manner. This assessment is designed to support students in developing and demonstrating CBT intervention skills through a role-play exercise that reflects real-world clinical practice.

For this task, you will submit a video recording (approximately 15 minutes) demonstrating the application of a CBT intervention with a role-play client. The role-play client may be a peer, colleague, friend, or family member.

At the beginning of the recording, you should provide a brief introduction outlining the client presentation, the CBT intervention being demonstrated, and any adaptations made to meet the needs of the client, population, or practice context.

The role play should focus on the delivery of a CBT intervention and may incorporate cognitive, behavioural, or integrated CBT strategies where appropriate.

Assessment Conditions

This assessment is intended to reflect authentic clinical practice. Students should focus on demonstrating a natural therapeutic interaction rather than delivering a scripted performance.

Students may prepare for the role play in advance; however, scripts, cue cards, AI-generated prompts, or other materials used to direct the interaction are not permitted during the recording. The recorded role play should reflect the student's own communication, clinical reasoning, and intervention skills.

Assessment Criteria

Detailed criteria and a more detailed rubric will be available to students on Blackboard.

You will be assessed on your:

  • Application of CBT intervention principles
  • Adaptation of CBT strategies to the client and context
  • Professional communication and therapeutic style
  • Clinical reasoning and intervention rationale
  • Demonstration of CBT skills within the role-play interaction

assessments.task_description:
Task Description

Effective CBT practice requires clinicians to develop knowledge and skills in assessment, formulation, treatment planning, intervention, and reflective practice. This assessment provides students with an opportunity to demonstrate their understanding and application of CBT principles through a professional discussion with the Course Coordinator, while reflecting on their development as an emerging CBT practitioner.

Students will participate in an individual 20-minute professional discussion (viva examination) conducted via Zoom during the examination period. The discussion will be guided by questions from the Course Coordinator and will draw upon the concepts and skills developed throughout the course. Questions may address CBT assessment, formulation, treatment planning, intervention strategies, clinical decision-making, and the adaptation of CBT approaches to different clients and practice contexts.

Throughout the discussion, students will have the opportunity to explain and justify their clinical reasoning, integrate relevant CBT theory and evidence, and critically reflect on their learning and development throughout the course. The professional discussion is designed to provide an authentic opportunity to demonstrate their understanding, application of CBT principles, and development as an emerging CBT practitioner.

Assessment Criteria

Detailed criteria and a more detailed rubric will be available to students on Blackboard.

You will be assessed on your ability to:

  • Demonstrate knowledge and application of CBT theory and practice.
  • Explain and justify clinical reasoning using CBT principles.
  • Critically reflect on your development as an emerging CBT practitioner.
  • Communicate ideas clearly, professionally, and effectively.
